γέρων: γέρων — old man; masc. nom. sg.

γεφύρας: γέφυρα — bridge; fem. acc. pl.; πολέμοιο γέφυραι is the open ground between armies (sense debated)
γλαυκῶπις: γλαυκῶπις — epithet of Athena: ’gleaming-eyed’ (or ’owl-eyed’; sense uncertain); fem. nom. sg.

δύω: δύο — two; numeral, epic by-form δύω, indeclinable
δὲ: δέ — and, but; connective particle · also the enclitic suffix -δε, ’to, toward’ (οἶκον δὲ ’homeward’)
δὴ: δή — indeed, now, in fact; emphatic particle
δῖα: δῖος — heavenly, divine, illustrious; fem. nom. sg., epithet of a noble woman

δῶκε: δίδωμι — give; aor. 3 sg. act., unaugmented (= Attic ἔδωκε)

εὐαίμονος: Εὐαίμων — Euaemon, father of Eurypylus; masc. gen. sg.
εὐρύπυλος: Εὐρύπυλος — Eurypylus, son of Euaemon, leader of the men of Ormenium; masc. nom. sg.
εὐχόμενος: εὔχομαι — pray, vow, boast; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’praying’ · also ’boasting’, of a claim
ζεὺς: Ζεύς — Zeus, king of the gods; nom. sg.

θυμός: θυμός — life, the life-breath that leaves the body; also heart, spirit; masc. nom. sg.
θώρηκος: θώραξ — breastplate, cuirass; masc. gen. sg., epic θώρηκ- (= Attic θώρακος)

κέντορες: κέντωρ — goader, driver (from κεντέω ’prick’); masc. nom. pl.

καμπύλα: καμπύλος — curved, bent; neut. acc. pl., with τόξα

κλέος: κλέος — fame, renown; neut. nom. sg., subject: ’fame’ · also neut. acc. sg., object: ’a report’
κλυτὸς: κλυτός — famous, renowned; adj., masc. nom. sg. · also the masc. form used with a fem. name, nom. sg., agreeing with Ἱπποδάμεια
κρατερὸν: κρατερός — strong, mighty (by-form of καρτερός); masc./neut. acc. sg.

κῆρα: κήρ — doom, fate of death; fem. acc. sg.
κῦδος: κῦδος — glory, the lustre of success granted by a god; neut. acc. sg. · also neut. nom. sg., in apposition: ’glory’
λαμπρὸν: λαμπρός — bright, shining; neut. nom./acc. sg.
λιπὼν: λείπω — leave, leave behind; aor. part. act. masc. nom. sg.: ’having left’
λυκάονος: Λυκάων — Lycaon, father of Pandarus; masc. gen. sg. · also Lycaon, a son of Priam and brother of Paris; masc. gen. sg.

μακρὸν: μακρός — long, tall, high; masc. acc. sg., agreeing with Ὄλυμπον · also neut. acc. sg. used adverbially with ἄϋσεν: ’loudly’
μεγάθυμοι: μεγάθυμος — great-hearted, high-spirited; masc. nom. pl.

μενέλαος: Μενέλαος — Menelaus, king of Sparta, brother of Agamemnon; masc. nom. sg.

μετάφρενον: μετάφρενον — the back (between the shoulders); neut. acc. sg.
μετὰ: μετά — among, with, after; + dat./acc./gen. · also an adverb, ’among them’, or a preverb in tmesis
μηριόνης: Μηριόνης — Meriones, Idomeneus’ Cretan comrade; masc. nom. sg.

νῆας: ναῦς — ship; fem. acc. pl., epic νῆας (= Attic ναῦς)

οὔρεσιν: ὄρος — mountain; neut. dat. pl., epic οὖρος, οὔρεσιν (= Attic ὄρεσιν)
οὔτ: οὔτε (elided οὔτ’) — nor, and not; correlative negative conj.
πάντα: πᾶς — all, every; neut. acc. pl.: ’all (things)’ · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with a name: ’all (through the whole of)’ (Αἰγιαλόν τ’ ἀνὰ πάντα)
πάσης: πᾶς — all, whole; fem. gen. sg., with μάχης
παλλὰς: Παλλάς — Pallas, a title of Athena; fem. nom. sg.

πεδίῳ: πεδίον — plain, flat land; neut. dat. sg.
περ: περ — even, though; enclitic particle, concessive or intensive; εἴ περ ’even if’
περικαλλέα: περικαλλής — very beautiful; masc. acc. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic περικαλλῆ), agreeing with δίφρον · also fem. acc. sg., agreeing with δειρήν: ’very beautiful’
πεσών: πίπτω — fall; aor. part. act. masc. nom. sg.: ’having fallen’
πικρὸν: πικρός — bitter, sharp; adj., masc. acc. sg., with ὀϊστόν
πικρὸς: πικρός — bitter, sharp; adj., masc. nom. sg., with ὀϊστός
πλεῖστοι: πολύς — much, many; superl. πλεῖστος, masc. nom. pl.: ’in the greatest numbers’
πολέες: πολύς — much, many; masc. nom. pl., epic πολέες (= Attic πολλοί)
πολλὰ: πολύς — much, many; neut. acc. pl.; also adverbial, ’much, earnestly’
πρίν: πρίν — before, sooner; adv.; and conj. + inf., ’before’; πρὶν … πρίν ’not … until’
προΐει: προΐημι — send forth, send off; impf. 3 sg. (προΐει, diaeresis marking the separate syllable)
προσέφη: πρόσφημι — speak to, address; aor. 3 sg.
προσηύδα: προσαυδάω — speak to, address; impf. 3 sg.
πρόσθ: πρόσθε — before, in front of; prep. + gen., elided πρόσθ’ (= πρόσθε): ’before (the others)’

πρὸ: πρό — before, forth; adv. or preverb, in tmesis (πρὸ … ἧκε = προῆκε ’sent forth’); also prep. + gen.

πυκιναὶ: πυκινός — close-packed, thick, close; fem. nom. pl.
πᾶσι: πᾶς — all, every; masc./neut. dat. pl.
πᾶσιν: πᾶς — all, every; masc./neut. dat. pl. (ν-movable)
σκαμάνδριον: Σκαμάνδριος — of the Scamander, Scamandrian; neut. acc. sg., agreeing with πεδίον
σκότος: σκότος — darkness; masc. nom. sg., the dark of death
στήθεσφιν: στῆθος — breast, chest; neut. in epic -φιν, a case ending serving as gen. or dat. (= Attic στήθους, στήθει); after ἀμφί: ’about the chest’
στῆθος: στῆθος — breast, chest; neut. acc. sg.
σχεδὸν: σχεδόν — near, close by; adv. (also + gen./dat.)
τ: τε (elided τ’) — and; ’epic τε’ also marks a general truth; in τ’ ἄρ with a question, ’then’ · also epic τε attached to ἦ, strengthening it: ἦ τ’ ’truly indeed’
τά: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. pl., ’those things’; accented before an enclitic · also relative, neut. nom. pl.: ’which’ (τά τ’ αἰδῶ ἀμφικαλύπτει ’which cover the shame’) · also neut. nom. pl. with a noun, article-like: ’the’ (τά τε δῶρ’ Ἀφροδίτης ’and the gifts of Aphrodite’) · also relative, neut. acc. pl.: ’which’ (τά οἵ ποτε … πόρε ’which he once gave him’)
τάμε: τέμνω — cut; aor. 3 sg. act., epic stem ταμ-, unaugmented (= Attic ἔτεμε): ’cut’
τε: τε — and, both...and; enclitic connective; also ’epic τε’ marking a standing general truth in relative clauses
τεύχε: τεῦχος — armour, gear (pl. τεύχεα); neut. nom. pl., elided (τεύχε’ = τεύχεα)
τι: τις, τι — someone, something; neut. nom./acc. sg. · in ὅ τι, ’whatever, why’ (= ὅτι) · also adverbial acc. with οὐ: ’at all’ (οὔ τι δυνήσεαι ’you will not at all be able’) · also adverbial acc. after εἰ: ’at all’ (εἴ ποτε δή τι … ὤνησας ’if ever you helped at all’) · also neut. acc. sg. with κακόν after μή: ’some’ (μή τι … ῥέξῃ κακὸν ’lest he do some evil’) · also adverbial acc. after μή: ’at all’ (μή τι διατρίβειν ’not to delay at all’)

τοῦ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it (in Homer a pronoun); masc. gen. sg., ’of him, him’ · also relative, ’whose’ · also with a noun, ’that’ (τοῦ βασιλῆος ’that king’)
τρώεσσι: Τρῶες — the Trojans; masc. dat. pl., epic -εσσι (= Attic Τρωσί)
τρώεσσιν: Τρῶες — Trojans; masc. dat. pl., epic -εσσιν (= Attic Τρωσί)
τρώων: Τρῶες — the Trojans; masc. gen. pl.
τρῶας: Τρῶες — the Trojans; masc. acc. pl.
τρῶες: Τρῶες — the Trojans; masc. nom. pl.
τυδέος: Τυδεύς — Tydeus, father of Diomedes; masc. gen. sg. (Τυδέος υἱός ’son of Tydeus’, periphrasis for Diomedes)
τόξα: τόξον — bow; neut. acc. pl. (plural for a single bow)
τότε: τότε — then, at that time; adv.
τώ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it (in Homer a pronoun); dual nom.: ’the two of them, they two’ (τώ γε) · also dual relative: ’the two who’ (τώ οἱ ἔσαν κήρυκε ’the two who were his heralds’) · also adverb (= Attic τῷ), ’therefore, so’ · also dual acc. relative: ’whom (the two)’ (τώ μοι … γείνατο ’whom … bore for me’)
τὸ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. sg., ’this, that’ · also relative, neut. nom. sg.: ’which’ (σκῆπτρον, τὸ … οὔ ποτε φύλλα φύσει) · also neut. acc. sg. with a noun, article-like: ’the, that’ (τὸ Πελασγικὸν Ἄργος ’the Pelasgian Argos’) · also neut. acc. sg. adverbial: ’on that account, therefore’ (τὸ καὶ κλαίουσα τέτηκα ’and so I waste away weeping’) · also τὸ πρῶτον, adverbial: ’at first’ (ὡς τὸ πρῶτον ’as at first’)
τὸν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. sg., ’him’; with a noun, ’that’ · also relative, ’whom’
τὼ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it (in Homer a pronoun); dual nom.: ’the two of them, those two’ · also dual acc.: ’those two’ (τὼ γὰρ νεικείεσκε) · also τὼ = τῷ, adv.: ’therefore, so’ (τὼ οὐκ ἂν … ἀγορεύοις) · also dual relative: ’whom’
τῷ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it (in Homer a pronoun); masc./neut. dat. sg., ’to him’ · also adverbial, ’therefore’ · also neut., ’on it’ (τῷ … ἐρεισάμενος ’leaning on it’) · also with a noun, ’that, the’ (ἤματι τῷ ’on that day’; τῷ δεκάτῳ ’in the tenth’) · also instrumental, ’with it’ (τῷ … τύψε ’struck with it’)
υἱέες: υἱός — son; masc. nom. pl., epic υἱέες (= Attic υἱεῖς)
υἷε: υἱός — son; masc. nom. dual: ’two sons’
φάλαγγας: φάλαγξ — line of battle, battle-line, phalanx; fem. acc. pl.
φάλαγγες: φάλαγξ — battle-line, line of battle; fem. nom. pl.
φημι: φημί — say, declare, assert; pres. 1 sg.
φυλεΐδης: Φυλεΐδης — son of Phyleus (patronymic); masc. nom. sg.
χαλκός: χαλκός — bronze; masc. nom. sg., also the bronze blade or spear-head
χαλκὸν: χαλκός — bronze; masc. acc. sg.: ’the bronze’ (i.e. armour) · also the bronze weapon, the spear-point: ’the bronze’ (χαλκὸν ἀνασχέσθαι ’to withstand the bronze’)
χειρὸς: χείρ — hand; fem. gen. sg.; χειρὸς ἑλόντε ’taking by the hand’ (gen. of the part seized)
χθονὸς: χθών — earth, ground; fem. gen. sg.: κατὰ χθονὸς ’down upon the ground’
ἀγαμέμνων: Ἀγαμέμνων — Agamemnon, king of Mycenae, leader of the Achaeans at Troy; masc. nom. sg.
ἀγλαὸς: ἀγλαός — splendid, radiant; masc. nom. sg.
ἀθήνη: Ἀθήνη — Athena, goddess of wisdom and war; nom. sg.
ἀλεξάνδρῳ: Ἀλέξανδρος — Alexander, another name of Paris; masc. dat. sg.
ἀλλ: ἀλλά (elided ἀλλ’) — but; well then · also ’except’: ’but only’ (ἀλλ’ οἶοι ’except us two’)
ἀλλήλοισιν: ἀλλήλων — one another; reciprocal pron., masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις): ’to one another’
ἀμύμων: ἀμύμων — blameless, excellent (an old epithet whose exact force is uncertain); masc./fem. nom. sg.
ἀν: ἀνά (elided ἀν’) — up, along, through; prep. + acc.: ’up through, throughout’
ἀντήνορος: Ἀντήνωρ — Antenor, a Trojan elder; masc. gen. sg.
ἀντικρὺ: ἀντικρύ — straight through, right through; adv. (epic, = ἀντικρύς)
ἀπὸ: ἀπό — from, away from; + gen. · also as preverb in tmesis, separated from its verb (ἀπὸ … ὀλέσσει = ἀπολέσει ’will destroy’; ἀπὸ … δοθείη = ἀποδοθείη ’be given back’)
ἀράβησε: ἀραβέω — clatter, rattle; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= Attic ἠράβησε)
ἀργείοισι: Ἀργεῖοι — Argives, Greeks; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οις)
ἀρχὸν: ἀρχός — leader, chief; masc. acc. sg.
ἀτρεΐδης: Ἀτρεΐδης — son of Atreus (patronymic); masc. nom. sg.
ἀτὰρ: ἀτάρ — but, and; epic conj. (by-form of αὐτάρ)
ἀχαιοὺς: Ἀχαιοί — the Achaeans, the Greeks; masc. acc. pl.
ἀχαιοῖς: Ἀχαιοί — the Achaeans, the Greeks; masc. dat. pl.
ἀχαιῶν: Ἀχαιοί — the Achaeans, the Greeks; gen. pl.
ἁλιζώνων: Ἁλιζῶνες — the Halizones, a people; masc. gen. pl.
ἂν: ἀνά — up, aboard; prep./preverb, with apocope ἂν before δ’; in tmesis (ἂν … βήσομεν ’put aboard’) · also modal particle ἄν (= κεν) written ἂν: with the opt., potential: ’would’; with the subj. after εὖτ’: ’whenever’ · also with ὡς + subj.: ’in the way that’ (ὡς ἂν ἐγὼ εἴπω ’as I may say’) · also modal particle with the subj. after ὅτ’: ’whenever’ (ὅτ’ ἂν … γένωνται ’whenever they come to be’) · also modal particle with a fut. or short-vowel subj.: ’could’ (οὐκ ἂν … μυθήσομαι ’I could not tell’) · also εἴ περ ἂν + opt., ’even if … should’ · also εἴ περ ἂν + subj., ’even if … ever’ (εἴ περ ἂν αὐτὸν σεύωνται ’even if they set upon him’) · also εἰ … ἂν + subj., ’if ever, should’ (εἰ δ’ ἂν … ἐθέλωσιν ’but if they should be unwilling’)
ἄναξ: ἄναξ — lord, master; masc. nom. sg. · also voc. sg. (same form), in address: ’lord!’ (κλῦθι, ἄναξ ’hear me, lord’)
ἄρ: ἄρα — then, so, as it seems; inferential particle, short form ἄρ (elided ἄρ’ before a vowel)
ἄρα: ἄρα — so, then, as it turned out; inferential particle
ἄρηα: Ἄρης — Ares, god of war; masc. acc. sg., epic (= Attic Ἄρη) · also by metonymy ’war’ (πολύδακρυν Ἄρηα ’tearful war’)
ἄριστος: ἀγαθός — good; superlative ἄριστος ’best’; adj., masc. nom. sg.
ἅλιον: ἅλιος — vain, to no purpose; masc. acc. sg., predicative with πόνον: ’vain’ · also neut. nom. sg., predicate: ’vain’ · also masc. acc. sg., attributive: ’vain’ · also neut. acc. sg., attributive: ’vain’ (ἅλιον βέλος ’a vain shaft’)
ἐΐσας: ἐΐσος (ἔΐσος) — equal, even, balanced (of ships, sense uncertain); fem. acc. pl., epic · also of mares, ’balanced, level’ (ἐπὶ νῶτον ἐΐσας ’balanced along the back’)
ἐκ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as adverb or preverb in tmesis, no case expressed: ’out’ (ἐκ δ’ ἔβαν ’and out they stepped’)
ἐλθὼν: ἔρχομαι — go, come; aor. part. act. masc. nom. sg.: ’having come’
ἐν: ἐν — in, on, among; + dat.; also used as an adverb, ’in it, there’ · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐν … βάλῃ = ἐμβάλῃ ’cast in’; ἐν … χεῦον = ἔγχεον ’pour in’)
ἐνόησε: νοέω — perceive, notice, think; aor. 3 sg. act., augmented: ’noticed’
ἐξ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐξ … ἕντο = ἐξέντο, from ἐξίημι ’send out, put away (desire)’)
ἐοικὼς: ἔοικα — be like, resemble (+ dat.); perf. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’like’
ἐπ: ἐπί (elided ἐπ’) — on, upon, over, at; + dat./acc./gen. · also + acc., ’to, towards’ (βῆ δ’ ἐπ’ Ἀτρεΐδην ’went to the son of Atreus’) · also + dat., ’to’ (πέμψαι ἐπ’ Ἀτρεΐδῃ ’to send to’) · also preverb in tmesis (ἐπ’ … θήσειν ’to lay upon’) · also + acc. of time, ’until, at’ (ἐπ’ ἠέλιον δῦναι ’until the sun sets’) · also + dat., ’against’ (ἐπ’ ἀλλήλοισιν ἰόντες ’coming against one another’) · also + gen., ’toward’ (ἐπ’ ὠκεανοῖο ῥοάων ’toward the streams of Oceanus’)
ἐπέεσσι: ἔπος — word, speech; neut. dat. pl., epic -εσσι (= Attic ἔπεσι)
ἐπὶ: ἐπί — on, upon, to, against; + dat./acc./gen.; also a preverb in tmesis (ἐπὶ … ἔτελλε = ἐπέτελλε) · also + dat., ’in aid of, on behalf of’ (ἐπὶ Τρώεσσιν ἀρῆξαι ’to help the Trojans’) · also + acc. of duration, ’for’ (ἐπὶ χρόνον ’for a time’) · also + acc. of extent, ’over, along’ (ἐπὶ νῶτον ’along the back’) · also + acc. of the thing aimed at, ’for’ (ἐπὶ τεύχεα ’for the armour’)
ἐσθλὸν: ἐσθλός — good, noble, brave; neut. acc. sg. · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with a masc. noun: ’good, brave’
ἐόντες: εἰμί — be; pres. part. masc. nom. pl., epic (= Attic ὄντες): ’being’
ἑλοῦσ: αἱρέω — take, take hold of; aor. part. act. fem. nom. sg., elided (ἑλοῦσ’ = ἑλοῦσα): ’taking’
ἔβαλ: βάλλω — throw, hit, strike; aor. 3 sg., elided (ἔβαλ’ = ἔβαλε): ’struck, hit’
ἔβαλε: βάλλω — throw, hit, strike; aor. 3 sg.: ’struck, hit’
ἔγχεϊ: ἔγχος — spear; neut. dat. sg., epic -εϊ (= Attic ἔγχει)
ἔην: εἰμί — be; impf. 3 sg., epic (= Attic ἦν)
ἔλασσεν: ἐλαύνω — drive, strike; aor. 3 sg., epic -σσ- (= Attic ἤλασε)
ἔλλαβε: λαμβάνω — take, seize, get; aor. 3 sg., augmented with double λ, epic (= Attic ἔλαβε)
ἔνθ: ἔνθα (elided ἔνθ’) — there, then; adverb of place or time
ἔπειτα: ἔπειτα — then, next, after that; adv.
ἔργα: ἔργον — deed, work; neut. nom./acc. pl. · also ’tilled land, farmland’ (ἔργα νέμοντο ’inhabited the farmlands’)
ἔρυτο: ἐρύομαι (ῥύομαι) — protect, ward off; impf. 3 sg. mid., epic (= Attic ἐρρύετο); an aorist sense (= ἐρρύσατο) is possible
ἔστη: ἵστημι — set, stand; aor. 3 sg. intrans.: ’stood, took his stand’
ἔτλη: τλάω — bring oneself to, dare, endure; aor. 3 sg. (ἔτλην, inf. τλῆναι)
ἔφατ: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid., augmented, elided (ἔφατ’ = ἔφατο)
ἕκαστος: ἕκαστος — each, every; masc. nom. sg.
ἕλε: αἱρέω — take, seize; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= Attic εἷλε)
ἠὲ: ἠέ — or; epic conj. (= Attic ἤ), correlative with ἠέ · also ’than’ after a comparative (γλυκίων … ἠὲ νέεσθαι ’sweeter than to go home’)
ἡγεμόνων: ἡγεμών — leader, guide; masc. gen. pl.: ’of the leaders’
ἡφαίστοιο: Ἥφαιστος — Hephaestus, god of the forge; by metonymy, fire; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
ἣ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. nom. sg. (grave, mid-clause form) · also demonstrative, ’she’ (ἣ δ’ … βεβήκει)
ἤριπε: ἐρείπω — throw down; in the intransitive aor. ἤριπον, fall headlong, crash down; aor. 3 sg.: ’fell headlong’
ἥφαιστος: Ἥφαιστος — Hephaestus, god of the forge; nom. sg.
ἦ: ἦ — truly, surely; affirming particle; ἦ μέν in oaths · also an interrogative particle · also ἠμί — say; impf. 3 sg. ἦ ’he said’, in ἦ καί, ἦ ῥα · also ἦ = ἤ, ’or’ (εἰ … ἦ ’whether … or’)
ἰδαῖος: Ἰδαῖος — Idaeus, herald of Priam; masc. nom. sg.
ἰδομενεὺς: Ἰδομενεύς — Idomeneus, king of Crete, leader of the Cretans at Troy; masc. nom. sg.
ἰδὲ: ἰδέ — and; epic conj. (= Attic καί)
ἰόντες: εἶμι — go, come; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’going, coming’
ἴδον: ὁράω — see; aor. 1 sg., unaugmented, from the root of εἶδον (= εἶδον): ’I saw’ · also aor. 3 pl., unaugmented (= εἶδον): ’they saw’
ἵν: ἵνα — where; relative adv. of place, elided (ἵν’ = ἵνα; = Attic οὗ) · also conj. ’so that’
ὀξέϊ: ὀξύς — sharp, keen; masc./neut. dat. sg., epic ὀξέϊ (= Attic ὀξεῖ)
ὀστέον: ὀστέον — bone; neut. acc. sg., uncontracted (= Attic ὀστοῦν)
ὀχέων: ὄχος — chariot, car (usually pl. ὄχεα); neut. gen. pl.
ὃ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he (in Homer a pronoun); masc. nom. sg., printed with a grave accent in some editions · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ, neut. nom./acc. sg., ’which’ · also neut. nom. sg. demonstrative: ’this’ (ὃ δέ τοι … ὅρκος ’and this shall be your oath’) · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ, masc. nom. sg.: ’who’ (ὃ σφῶϊ προΐει ’who sent you’) · also masc. nom. sg. in the correlative ὃ μὲν … ὃ δέ: ’the one … the other’
ὃς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg. · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own (masc. nom. sg.) · also plain demonstrative, ’he’ (ὃς γὰρ δεύτατος ἦλθεν), not a relative
ὄρνυτο: ὄρνυμι — rouse; mid. rise, rush; impf. 3 sg. mid., unaugmented (= Attic ὤρνυτο): ’rose, rushed’
ὄσσε: ὄσσε — the two eyes; neut. dual noun, no sg., epic (= Attic ὄμματα)
ὄχεσφι: ὄχος — chariot, car; neut. instrumental case in -φι (= dat. pl. ὄχεσι): ’with chariots’
ὅθι: ὅθι — where; epic relative adverb (= Attic οὗ)
ὅς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg., accented before an enclitic · also ὅς τις as an indirect interrogative: ’who’ (ὅς τις ὅδ’ ἐστίν ’who this is’)
ὑπ: ὑπό (elided ὑπ’) — under, beneath; + gen.: ’from under’ (ὑπ’ ἀνθερεῶνος) · also + gen. of the agent or cause, ’under’ (ἀϋσάντων ὑπ’ Ἀχαιῶν ’as the Achaeans shouted’) · also prep. + dat. with τίκτω, of the father: ’to’ (ὑπ’ Ἀδμήτῳ τέκε ’bore to Admetus’) · also + dat., ’under’ (ὑπ’ ἠελίῳ ’under the sun’)
ὑπὲρ: ὑπέρ — over, beyond; + gen.: ’on behalf of’ (ὑπὲρ Δαναῶν) · also + acc., ’beyond’ (ὑπὲρ αἶσαν ’beyond due measure’) · also + gen. of place, ’above’ (στέρνον ὑπὲρ μαζοῖο ’the breast above the nipple’)
ὑπὸ: ὑπό — under, beneath; adv. and preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ὑπὸ … τάνυσσαν ’stretched under’) · also prep. + acc. of motion: ’to, under’ (ὑπὸ Ἴλιον ἦλθον ’came to Ilios’) · also prep. + dat., ’under, beneath’ (ὑπὸ πλατανίστῳ ’beneath a plane-tree’) · also prep. + dat. with τίκτω, of the father: ’to’ (ὑπὸ Πειριθόῳ τέκετο ’bore to Peirithous’) · also prep. + gen.: ’beneath, from under’ (ὑπὸ στέρνοιο ’beneath the breast’) · also prep. + gen. of cause: ’under (the blast of)’ (ὑπὸ Ζεφύροιο ἰωῆς)
ὑσμίνην: ὑσμίνη — battle, fight; fem. acc. sg.
ὕστερος: ὕστερος — later, younger; comparative, masc. nom. sg., predicate: ’younger’
ὠκεανοῖο: Ὠκεανός — Ocean, the river encircling the earth; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -οῦ)
ὡς: ὡς — as, how, that; conj. (unaccented) introducing a fact: ’that’ · also causal: ’since, seeing that’ · also temporal, ’when’ (ὡς ἴδον ’when they saw’) · also final, ’so that’ (+ subj./opt.): ὡς φρήτρη … ἀρήγῃ ’so that clan may help clan’ · also introducing a wish, with ὄφελεν: ’would that’ (ὡς ὄφελεν θάνατός μοι ἁδεῖν ’would that death had pleased me’) · also in a comparison, ’like, just as’ (ὡς ὅδε οἶνος ’like this wine’)
ὣς: ὥς — thus, so; adverb (accented, distinct from unaccented ὡς ’as’; = Attic οὕτως); ὣς ἔφατ’ ’so he spoke’ · also ὣς = ὡς, ’like, as’ after its noun (κακὸν ὣς ’like a coward’)
ὦκα: ὦκα — quickly, swiftly; adv., from ὠκύς
ὦρσε: ὄρνυμι — stir up, rouse; aor. 3 sg. act., transitive: ’roused’
ὦρσεν: ὄρνυμι — rouse, raise up; aor. 3 sg. act., augmented, with movable ν (= ὦρσε)
ὦσε: ὠθέω — push, thrust; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= Attic ἔωσε): ’thrust’
ᾔδη: οἶδα — know; plpf. 3 sg. with past sense (= impf.): ’knew’
ᾗσιν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; fem. dat. pl., epic ᾗσιν (= ἑῇσιν)
ᾧ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative, masc./neut. dat. sg.: ’to whom’ · also possessive, ’his own’
ῥα: ἄρα — then, so; weak enclitic form ῥα (used after a vowel)
